doc_name: Leslie Fox Prize for Numerical Analysis
text: The Leslie Fox Prize for Numerical Analysis, established in 1985 by the Institute of Mathematics and its Applications (IMA), is a biennial award created in honour of the mathematician Leslie Fox (1918–1992). It recognizes "young numerical analysts worldwide" who are under 31 years of age. Candidates submit papers for evaluation by a committee, which then selects shortlisted individuals to present lectures at the Leslie Fox Prize meeting. The prize is awarded in two categories—First Prize and Second Prize—based on a combination of mathematical and algorithmic brilliance as well as presentational skills.
